page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance architecture utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The hardware is configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8175M processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz with two threads per core. System memory comprises 256 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, establishing a proportional 1:4 vCPU-to-memory profile of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is non-local, meaning instances rely entirely on remote network volumes. The instance provides a 20 Gbps baseline network throughput and includes no discrete GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements demonstrate distinct performance profiles between single-threaded and parallelized tasks. Single-core processing metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, reflect baseline execution speeds common to its processor generation. In contrast, multi-threaded benchmarks demonstrate consistent throughput across all 64 vCPUs, evidenced by average multi-core scores in PassMark and stress-ng. PassMark extended instruction metrics demonstrate elevated capability due to support for AVX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory subsystem testing highlights particularly high uncached memory bandwidth, with large-block sequential read rates measuring 192.72 GB/sec and write rates achieving 90.92 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the m5.16xlarge provides dense multi-core parallel capacity coupled with high memory throughput without the resource premium associated with dedicated memory-optimized instance families. A primary technical tradeoff is the absence of integrated NVMe storage, meaning I/O-intensive workloads rely on external storage performance limits and network latency. Additionally, single-thread-bound applications may experience bottlenecking compared to newer high-frequency compute-optimized platforms. Given these specifications, the server is suitable for medium to large enterprise applications, distributed caching layers such as Redis clusters, batch compilation, static web infrastructure, and container orchestration nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Nitro hypervisor, featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8175M processor running at 3.1 GHz. It integrates 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and includes no dedicated GPUs, while offering a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps. Benchmark evaluation shows modest single-core throughput alongside balanced multi-core computation and elevated uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 192.72 GB/sec read and 90.92 GB/sec write. Extended instruction support via AVX-512 contributes to strong vector operations. Due to its large memory capacity, multi-core scaling, and predictable network bandwidth, m5.16xlarge is well aligned with memory-resident caching layers, container clusters, multi-threaded batch jobs, and enterprise database servers relying on remote persistent storage.
